item.title: Milence opens truck charging hub with four MCS chargers in Belgium
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Milence brings its 39th charging hub online. The location in Temse is now the joint venture's fifth truck charging park in Belgium. In addition to four CCS charging points with up to 400 kW of charging power, Temse also features four megawatt charging points capable of delivering up to 1,500 kW.

item.title: Republic of Moldova presents national eMobility roadmap
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Republic of Moldova has established a national eMobility programme which aims to expand the charging network to 600 public charging points by the end of the decade and electrifying 15 per cent of the vehicle fleet.

item.title: Fraunhofer researchers aim to unlock the potential of lithium-metal anodes
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Researchers from two Fraunhofer Institutes are exploring new approaches to improving the performance and lifespan of battery systems. One idea is to use lithium itself as an active anode material in lithium-metal anodes, thereby achieving higher specific capacity in battery cells.

item.title: India: Jindal Stainless deploys 10 electric heavy-duty trucks
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Indian steel manufacturer Jindal Stainless has added ten heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. For the first time, the company is using electric trucks to transport finished goods, building on its earlier introduction of alternative-fuel vehicles running on LNG and CNG.

item.title: New autonomous fleet coordination approach aims to tackle rush-hour traffic
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Researchers at Sweden's Chalmers University have developed an optimisation method to more efficiently guide autonomous electric taxis through urban traffic. The approach combines AI forecasts with mathematical models and is designed to account for unpredictable factors such as unusual weather conditions.

item.title: Australia to fund 130-vehicle commercial V2G trial
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) has committed AU$4 million to a project which will deploy vehicle-to-grid technology across a fleet of 130 EVs. The three-year project aims to explore whether fleets can reduce operating costs by providing grid services without compromising on day-to-day operations.

item.title: Chery launches megawatt charging system for passenger EVs
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In China, Chery has entered the megawatt charging race. Following the introduction of megawatt charging solutions by BYD, Geely, and Huawei, the state-owned automaker now presents a charger with 1.44 MW peak output.

item.title: VW ‘centralising’ ADAS development under Audi’s leadership
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Volkswagen is apparently establishing a unit called 'OneTeam' to accelerate the development of driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving. Cariad manager Manuel Birke will reportedly take over the leadership and will report to Audi development board member Rouven Mohr in the future.

item.title: BAIC and CATL aim to accelerate battery swap approach
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Chinese automakers BAIC Group and CATL are deepening their partnership in the field of passenger car battery swapping: BAIC plans to develop more compatible models and advance the construction of swapping stations with the help of its dealer network.

item.title: Price reduction at market launch: Jetta M6 enters the Chinese market
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: VW's sub-brand is launching the Jetta M6 at dealerships in China. With the market launch, the manufacturer is also adjusting the pre-sale prices downward by 1,000 yuan (~€134 euros). Read on for more details on what makes this mid-size sedan stand out, along with key data for the three available versions.

item.title: Canada freezes CO2 standards for passenger cars until 2029
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Canada's government is freezing fleet emission standards for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles at 2026 levels through 2029. This move aims to give automakers more flexibility. However, annual tightening of standards will resume starting with the 2030 model year.

item.title: Bosch faces radical corporate restructuring amid competitive pressures
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: The Bosch Group is undergoing an internal corporate restructuring. From August 1, 2027, the Mobility business sector will exist as an independent subsidiary, among others. Three additional areas will also be transferred to subsidiary companies. The group aims to enhance its competitiveness and operate with greater flexibility.

item.title: Mercedes in high demand as six-month lead time for CLA and GLC
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is surprised by the high demand for its all-electric models CLA and GLC. Currently, the delivery time for both vehicles is six months. The battery plant in Kamenz has been operating six days a week in a three-shift system since June to secure the supply of traction batteries.

item.title: EU Auto Package: Committee votes to relax CO₂ rules
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: In the European Parliament, standing committees have voted on the Auto Package. The votes are seen as an indicator of whether and to what extent the so-called combustion engine ban in the EU will be softened. The result: a majority of the Industry and Transport Committees are in favour of relaxing the CO2 rules, which the so-called centrist platform had internally agreed upon shortly before.

item.title: First drive in the Xpeng L03: finally a Chinese EV that doesn’t beep
item.dc:creator: Robin Engelhardt
item.description: With the L03, Xpeng brings its established strengths to a new price and size segment. Particularly in the Ultra variant, its equipment goes well beyond what many rivals offer. Given its competitive pricing, the occasional shortcoming we identified during our first test drive is easier to overlook. Deliveries in Europe are scheduled to begin later this year.

item.title: Audi China appoints Jeff Zhang and Rolf Michl as new dual leadership
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Audi is reshaping its leadership team for its China business. Starting in November, Jeff Zhang will replace Johannes Roschek as President of Audi China. Additionally, Rolf Michl, previously CEO of Audi Sport GmbH, will move to China as Chief Operating Officer.

item.title: Holger Scherr leaves Daimler Truck for SuperPanther
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Chinese e-truck manufacturer SuperPanther has appointed Dr. Holger Scherr to its European management team. Scherr will serve as Executive Vice President Europe, overseeing the establishment and expansion of the company's European operations. The appointment is a coup for SuperPanther, as Scherr joins the startup from Daimler Truck.

item.title: London considers mandating BEVs for new ride-hailing licences
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Transport for London (TfL) has launched a consultation on stricter licensing rules for ride-hailing services, such as Uber. TfL is considering requiring all newly licensed vehicles to be fully electric from 2028. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles would have a transition period until July 2030.

item.title: Electrify America opens its largest EV charging station to date
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The new charging site has opened in Orlando, Florida, and features 24 DC fast chargers capable of delivering up to 350 kW each. It's located at the Sand Lake Corners South shopping centre and serves both local drivers and visitors travelling to nearby attractions, including Disney World and Universal Studios.

item.title: India: Switch Mobility starts fulfilling 50-unit intercity electric bus order
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Switch Mobility has delivered six intercity electric buses to Purple Bus, the operating brand of Pune (Maharashtra)-based Indian private bus operator Prasanna Purple Mobility Solutions. These buses form the first batch of a 50-unit order the company announced in August.

item.title: Greater range at the same weight: silicon battery passes laboratory test
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: A critical breakthrough in battery research saw film cells with silicon-rich anodes endure over 1,000 cycles in testing without dropping below 80 per cent capacity. We explore the parameters that play a key role and what this progress could mean for electric vehicles.

item.title: Nvidia embraces European automakers
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Nvidia is expanding its business with technologies for automated driving in Europe. For example, the ridesharing service Bolt is relying on the Alpamayo stack from the AI company for its planned robotaxis, and VWN is showcasing the ID. Buzz AD with Nvidia Hyperion. At the same time, Volkswagen, Porsche, and other partners are advancing a joint data and simulation platform.

item.title: GM announces new efficient EV platform
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: GM has streamlined its development processes and introduced a new platform in a shorter timeframe, with the first production vehicles set to debut "very soon". From 2028, vehicles on the platform will also feature significantly more efficient batteries and a faster, centralised computing system.

item.title: Bosch bets on electric drives for trucks – while still backing hydrogen
item.dc:creator: Peter Schwierz
item.description: Bosch sees significant growth potential in the commercial vehicle sector and aims to broadly support the technological transformation of trucks. At the IAA Transportation, Jan-Oliver Röhrl, Executive Vice President Commercial Vehicles and Off-Road at Bosch, spoke with electrive about e-axles, the lack of charging infrastructure, hydrogen - and why Europe should not rule out options too early when it comes to new technologies.

item.title: CATL’s Akin Li: “Whichever battery type the market demands, we’ll have it”
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: CATL is a near-indispensable supplier to the emerging European e-truck industry, with many model series from local manufacturers running on cells or entire battery packs from the Chinese company. We met with CATL’s top manager Akin Li to explore how CATL plans to further strengthen its partnerships with Europe’s truck manufacturers.

item.title: BEV registrations rose sharply across Europe in September
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Registrations of electric cars in the EU rose sharply in September. According to ACEA, 290,117 pure electric cars were newly registered - 72.9 per cent more than in the same month last year. This put their market share at 29.9 per cent in September. Since the beginning of the year, BEVs have achieved a market share of 22.7 per cent.

item.title: Tesla Q3 results: full order books, but declining figures
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Tesla's revenue is stagnating, with the US electric car manufacturer witnessing a significant drop in profits during the third quarter. However, the Americans' car business is not doing poorly - order books are full. The reasons lie elsewhere.

item.title: Vilnius secures major loan for public transport electrification
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: VVT, the public transport operator for Vilnius, continues to electrify its fleet. Thanks to €110 million from the CEB and EIB, the city can introduce 161 emission-free buses and the requisite charging infrastructure.

item.title: New rules make it much easier to install cross-pavement EV chargers in England
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: Drivers in England can now install cross-pavement EV chargers without the need for planning permission, thanks to new permitted development rights. The government estimates the change could save households up to £300 in installation costs.

item.title: BYD adopts same partner as BMW for CKD assembly in Malaysia
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: BYD has decided to collaborate with contract manufacturer Inokom on local assembly of electric cars in Malaysia. The decision is likely due to significantly tightened import conditions. Inokom is also the local manufacturer of the BMW i5 for the Malaysian market.
